statement: Let \(p(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n)\) be a polynomial with integer coefficients. For each positive integer \(r\), let \(k(r)\) be the number of \(n\)-tuples \((a_1, \ldots, a_n)\) with \(0 \leq a_i \leq r-1\) and \(\gcd(p(a_1,\ldots,a_n), r) = 1\). Show that if \(u\) and \(v\) are coprime then \(k(uv) = k(u)k(v)\), and if \(p\) is prime then \(k(p^s) = p^{n(s-1)}k(p)\).
Given a point \(p\) inside a convex polyhedron \(P\), show that there is a face \(F\) of \(P\) such that the foot of the perpendicular from \(p\) to the plane of \(F\) lies in the interior of \(F\).

Two players alternate. The first player is given a pair of positive integers \((x_1, y_1)\). Each player replaces the pair \((x_n, y_n)\) by \((x_{n+1}, y_{n+1})\) where \(x_{n+1} = \min(x_n, y_n)\) and \(y_{n+1} = \max(x_n, y_n) - k \cdot x_{n+1}\) for some positive integer \(k\). The first player to pass on a pair with \(y_{n+1} = 0\) wins. For which values of \(x_1/y_1\) does the first player have a winning strategy?

Given points \(A_1(x_1,y_1,z_1), \ldots, A_n(x_n,y_n,z_n)\), let \(P(x,y,z)\) minimize \(\sum(|x-x_i|+|y-y_i|+|z-z_i|)\). Give an example (for each \(n > 4\)) of points \(A_i\) for which \(P\) lies outside the convex hull of the \(A_i\).

\(A\) and \(B\) wish to divide a triangular prism (triangular faces horizontal) into two pieces. \(A\) chooses a point \(P\) on the top face; \(B\) then chooses a vertical plane through \(P\) to cut the cake and takes the larger piece. Which point \(P\) should \(A\) choose to secure as large a slice as possible?
